title: Company-wide policies and processes: access, change, data, procurement, vendors, travel, templates
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and process guidance for: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel policies, and internal templates. It is intended to provide a single reference for employees and managers to understand minimum controls, approval flows, owners, and where to find templates and forms.

Scope

Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and vendors accessing company systems or performing work on behalf of Redwood. Specific sections identify teams responsible for enforcement and exceptions.

Contents (high level)
- Access & Permissions
- Change Management
- Data Management
- Procurement & Expenses
- Vendor Management & Onboarding
- Travel Policies & Reimbursement
- Internal Templates & Forms

1) Access & Permissions

Objective: Ensure least-privilege access, timely access changes, and traceable approvals.

Primary owners: Security & People Ops (Identity team + IT).

Policy summary:
- Role-based access: All production systems use role-based access control (RBAC). Engineers are granted developer roles by default; elevated privileges (prod-admin, infra-admin) require manager + security approval.
- Onboarding: New hires receive baseline access within 24 business hours. Baseline access includes email, SSO, and the developer sandbox. Production access requires explicit request via the access request form and a documented justification.
- Access review: Every team must complete quarterly access reviews for privileged roles. Teams must attest in the access review tracker.
- Temporary access: Temporary elevated access must be timebounded (max 7 days) and requested via the ticketing system with the start/end dates.
- Offboarding: Managers must submit deprovisioning requests to IT on the employee termination date. Access is revoked same day for terminated employees; for planned departures, accounts are disabled at close-of-business on the last date.

Required approvals and flows:
1. Requestor fills Access Request form (link to template).
2. Manager approves (email or ticket).
3. Security approves for privileged scopes.
4. IT implements and records change in audit log.

Example table of owners:
| Area | Owner team | SLA | Notes |
| Production access | Eng-SRE / Security | 1 business day for approval; implementation depends on infra | Prod-admin requires security review |
| Vendor access | IT + vendor manager | 2 business days | Must be on allowlist and time-bounded |

2) Change Management

Objective: Control changes to production systems to minimize outages and enable rapid rollback.

Scope: All changes that affect customer-facing services, infra configuration, deployment pipelines, or database schemas.

Standards:
- Change classification: standard (low-risk repeatable), normal (requires approval), emergency (fast path with retroactive review).
- Approval gates: Normal changes require a change ticket with owner, risk assessment, rollback plan, and scheduled maintenance window. Approvals by service owner and Eng-SRE are required.
- Canary & rollout: For model or runtime changes, use canary rollout with metrics thresholds defined in the change ticket (error rate, latency, throughput). Minimum canary duration: 30 minutes unless otherwise approved.
- Change freeze windows: Major release freeze windows are published in the roadmap; critical fixes may be allowed with executive approval.

Change process (numbered):
1. Create change ticket in the change tracker with impact analysis.
2. Eng-SRE reviews for risk and scheduling.
3. Service owner approves and schedules.
4. Execute change during approved window, monitor defined metrics.
5. If thresholds exceeded, rollback immediately and open post-change review.

3) Data Management

Objective: Protect customer and internal data, define retention, classification, and handling requirements.

Key policies:
- Data classification: Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted. All datasets must be labeled.
- Access controls: Sensitive datasets (Confidential/Restricted) require additional approvals and encryption at rest and in transit.
- Retention: Default retention for logs is 90 days; longer retention requires business justification and approval from security and legal.
- Backups: Critical data backed up daily; recovery tests performed quarterly.
- Data transfers: Cross-border transfers must follow data residency guidelines and be authorized by Legal.

Data handling checklist for teams:
- Document dataset classification and owner.
- Ensure encryption (KMS) for Confidential/Restricted data.
- Limit dataset access to least privilege and log all access.
- Maintain retention and deletion schedule.

4) Procurement & Expenses

Objective: Standardize buying, approval thresholds, and expense reimbursement to control spend and ensure compliance.

Procurement thresholds & approvers:
- < $1,000: Manager approval (credit card or purchase order).
- $1,000–$25,000: Department head approval + procurement team notification.
- > $25,000: Procurement + Finance + Legal review; multi-month contracts require executive sponsor.
- Capital purchases and multi-year commitments require Finance forecasting and Board-level notice when material.

Process highlights:
1. Use the Purchase Request template for any vendor or spend > $1,000.
2. Obtain at least two vendor quotes for purchases > $10,000 unless pre-approved preferred vendor.
3. Procurement team reviews vendor for terms, SLAs, and compliance.
4. Finance issues PO and sets payment terms.

Expenses and reimbursement:
- Employee-paid business expenses require submission within 30 days with receipts. Use the Expenses template (link) and categorize by card vs personal payment.
- Per diem for travel follows the published country tables; exceptions require manager approval.

5) Vendor Management & Onboarding

Objective: Ensure vendors meet security, legal, and performance standards before receiving access or sensitive data.

Vendor onboarding checklist:
- Completed Vendor Intake form and contract signed by Legal.
- Security questionnaire completed and reviewed. High-risk vendors (access to customer or restricted data) require SOC2/ISO evidence.
- Defined access scope and duration; all vendor accounts are time-bounded and monitored.
- Key contacts, escalation paths, and SLA definitions documented.

Renewal & offboarding:
- Contracts reviewed 60 days prior to renewal by the vendor owner.
- Offboarding plan must include account revocation, data return/destruction verification, and final invoice reconciliation.

6) Travel Policies & Reimbursement

Objective: Provide clear guidance for business travel, safety, and reimbursements while controlling costs.

Booking & approval:
- All business travel requires pre-approval from the employee's manager. Use the Travel Request template.
- Preferred booking channels (company travel portal) should be used to enforce corporate rates.

Allowable expenses and caps:
- Flights: Economy class for flights < 8 hours; premium economy or business requires exec approval.
- Hotels: Up to mid-tier business hotels; maximum nightly rates by city published in the travel matrix.
- Meals: Per diem or actuals with receipts; alcohol reimbursed only with manager approval for client dinners.

Reimbursement process:
1. Submit travel expense report within 15 days of return with receipts attached.
2. Manager approves; Finance processes reimbursement within next payroll cycle.

Safety & duty of care:
- Employees traveling to high-risk areas must notify People Ops and complete the travel risk assessment. Company-provided emergency contact and insurance details apply.

7) Internal Templates & Forms

This section lists commonly used templates and where to find them in the docs library. All templates live in the Templates space and are maintained by People Ops or Finance where noted.

Core templates (links are internal Confluence references):
- Access Request form (People Ops)
- Change Request / Change Ticket (Eng-SRE)
- Purchase Request (Procurement)
- Vendor Intake form (Legal/Procurement)
- Travel Request & Expense form (People Ops / Finance)
- Data Classification and Dataset Onboarding form (Security)

Governance & exceptions

Exceptions to these policies must be requested via the Exceptions Request form, documented with rationale, compensating controls, and an expiration. Exceptions are reviewed by the appropriate owner team and Security/Legal where applicable.

Audit and compliance

- Teams are responsible for maintaining artifacts (approval emails, tickets, signed contracts) for audits.
- Security and Finance conduct annual compliance checks (access reviews, procurement compliance, vendor evidence).

Contacts and escalation

- People Ops (policy owner): people-ops@redwood.com
- Procurement & Finance: procurement@redwood.com / finance@redwood.com
- Security & IT: security@redwood.com / it-support@redwood.com
- Legal: legal@redwood.com

Appendix: Quick checklists

Access request quick checklist:
- [ ] Manager approval
- [ ] Justification & scope defined
- [ ] Security approval for elevated scopes
- [ ] Implementation recorded in audit log

Procurement quick checklist:
- [ ] Purchase Request completed
- [ ] Two quotes where required
- [ ] Contract reviewed by Legal (if applicable)
- [ ] PO issued by Finance

Vendor offboarding checklist:
- [ ] Access revoked
- [ ] Data returned/destroyed verified
- [ ] Final invoice reconciled
